version.changelog: Create and bind a dedicated Telegram group per agent with isolated workspace provisioning; asks for model and init-file preferences, supports custom/default group naming, and enforces no-mention reply setup.

llm.summary: The skill largely does what it claims (provision an OpenClaw agent and bind a Telegram group) but contains several implementation inconsistencies and risky assumptions (hardcoded user paths, writes to the user's OpenClaw config without declaring it) that you should review before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the provided scripts and SKILL.md: both configure ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, create a workspace, and add a Telegram binding. Those actions are appropriate for a 'create agent + telegram group' skill. However, the scripts assume a particular filesystem layout (hardcoded /Users/yao defaults) which is not explained in the high-level description and is not appropriate for general users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructions remain within the stated scope (read models from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, create workspace, bind group, verify no-mention replies). It also instructs API-first Telegram actions and browser fallback; no automation code is included for those steps, so the operator/agent will need to perform or request manual actions. The instructions require reading and writing the OpenClaw config file (which can contain sensitive auth info), but they do not instruct collecting unrelated system data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present and the skill is instruction-first with two small Python scripts bundled. Nothing is downloaded or executed from remote URLs, and no package installation is required.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but it reads and overwrites the user's OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) and creates agent/workspace paths. The script defaults to /Users/yao as workspace-root and constructs agentDir with that hardcoded path, which is disproportionate and brittle. Because the OpenClaw config can contain auth/profile information, the skill's silent read/write of that file should have been declared and justified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and cannot autonomously gain platform-level persistence. It does modify the user's OpenClaw configuration file (a normal and expected action for provisioning), which is a privileged filesystem operation; that is acceptable for the stated purpose but should be made explicit to users.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill mostly does what it says, but review before running: 1) The scripts read and overwrite ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json — back that file up first since it may contain auth profiles and tokens. 2) The provision script uses /Users/yao as a default workspace-root and builds agentDir with that path; if your account is not 'yao' the script will still write that value into the config (a likely bug). Run the script with --workspace-root pointing at your actual home (e.g., --workspace-root "$HOME") or edit the script to use os.path.expanduser('~') instead. 3) init_workspace.py writes placeholder USER.md content that includes an odd default ("Name: Sexy", "Preferred language: Chinese"); check and replace defaults before creating agent workspaces. 4) The skill expects Telegram API or browser automation for group creation but contains no automation code — be prepared to perform manual steps or supply a separate integration tool. 5) If you need higher assurance: ask the author to (a) remove hardcoded /Users/yao, (b) document exactly what in openclaw.json will be read/changed, and (c) avoid surprising defaults in generated files. If you cannot obtain those clarifications, treat this as untrusted code and run it in an isolated environment after backing up your OpenClaw config.
